title: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing in Alzheimer's Disease: Targeting APOE4 Variants
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) affects over 50 million people worldwide, with the APOE4 allele conferring significant genetic risk. We developed a CRISPR-Cas9 based approach to correct APOE4 to the neutral APOE3 variant in human iPSC-derived neurons. Our results demonstrate 89% editing efficiency with minimal off-target effects (<0.1%), reduced amyloid-beta aggregation by 67%, and improved neuronal survival by 43% compared to controls. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed restoration of lipid metabolism pathways disrupted by APOE4. This study provides proof-of-concept for in vivo gene editing as a therapeutic strategy for AD, with lipid nanoparticle delivery enabling CNS penetration in a primate model.

title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Vaccines: Phase II Trial Results in Advanced Melanoma
abstract: Personalized mRNA vaccines encoding tumor-specific neoantigens represent a breakthrough in cancer immunotherapy. We conducted a Phase II randomized controlled trial in 156 advanced melanoma patients comparing personalized mRNA vaccine plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone. The vaccine group showed 78% objective response rate versus 45% in the control arm. Complete responses were observed in 31% of vaccine recipients. The vaccine was manufactured in 28 days from tumor biopsy using an AI-driven neoantigen prediction pipeline. Treatment-related adverse events were manageable. These results establish personalized mRNA vaccines as a paradigm-shifting approach to solid tumor immunotherapy.

title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Novel Microglia Sub-populations in Neuroinflammation
abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of multiple neurodegenerative diseases, yet the cellular heterogeneity of brain-resident immune cells remains poorly characterized. Using single-cell RNA sequencing of 485,000 microglia from human post-mortem brain tissue across 12 neurological conditions, we identified 12 novel microglia sub-populations including disease-associated microglia (DAM), interferon-responsive microglia (IRM), and a previously unknown proliferative microglia state (ProM). ProM cells show unique metabolic reprogramming and phagocytic activity. Trajectory analysis reveals that ProM represents a transitional state between homeostatic and DAM phenotypes. These findings provide a comprehensive atlas of microglial states and identify new therapeutic targets for neuroinflammatory diseases.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction in Multi-Omics Data
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTI) is a critical bottleneck in drug discovery. We present DrugGNN, a heterogeneous graph neural network that integrates protein-protein interactions, drug chemical structures, genomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics data within a unified knowledge graph of 2.4 million nodes and 18 million edges. DrugGNN achieves AUROC of 0.97 on the benchmark ChEMBL dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by 12%. Applied to 4,200 FDA-approved drugs against 847 understudied cancer targets, we identified 23 high-confidence repurposing candidates. Three candidates were experimentally validated in patient-derived organoids, showing IC50 values in the nanomolar range. DrugGNN reduces initial drug-target screening from months to 72 hours.

title: Long-Read Sequencing Resolves Complex Structural Variants in ALS Patients
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) has a complex genetic architecture, with 30% of familial cases and 10% of sporadic cases carrying known causative mutations. Previous short-read sequencing studies missed large structural variants (SVs) due to repetitive regions. Using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing on 1,200 ALS patients and 800 controls, we detected 3.8 times more SVs than previous studies. We identified 47 ALS-associated SVs, including expansions in C9orf72, ATXN2, and a novel expansion in the NIPA1 locus affecting 8.2% of sporadic ALS cases. Phase-resolved haplotypes revealed complex compound heterozygous variants missed by standard analysis. These findings redefine the genetic architecture of ALS and provide immediate diagnostic value.

title: Organoid-Based Drug Screening Platform for Pancreatic Cancer Chemoresistance
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a 5-year survival rate below 12% due to late diagnosis and chemoresistance. We developed a patient-derived organoid (PDO) biobank from 312 PDAC patients and created an automated high-throughput screening platform testing 4,800 drug combinations. Machine learning analysis of drug response patterns revealed 6 molecular subtypes of PDAC with distinct chemosensitivity profiles. A Wnt pathway inhibitor plus gemcitabine combination showed synergistic activity in 40% of PDOs corresponding to a mesenchymal subtype. Patients in the matched cohort receiving this combination showed 2.3-fold improvement in progression-free survival. This study establishes PDOs as predictive biomarkers for personalized PDAC therapy.

title: Gut Microbiome Modulation Enhances Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response
abstract: The gut microbiome significantly influences anti-tumor immunity, yet mechanisms connecting microbial composition to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy remain unclear. We performed longitudinal metagenomic profiling of 680 cancer patients treated with anti-PD-1 therapy, identifying a 'responsive microbiome signature' (RMS) characterized by enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, and Bifidobacterium species. Germ-free mice colonized with RMS showed 3.2-fold higher ICI response rates. A randomized trial of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from ICI responders to non-responders resulted in 32% of non-responders becoming responders. Mechanistically, RMS bacteria promote CXCL10 secretion, driving CD8+ T cell tumor infiltration.

title: AI-Driven Protein Structure Prediction Enables Rapid Antibody Engineering
abstract: Antibody engineering traditionally requires lengthy iterative cycles of design, expression, and testing. We present AbDesign, an AI system combining AlphaFold2 structure prediction, diffusion-based CDR loop generation, and reinforcement learning optimization to design antibodies with specified binding properties. AbDesign generates 10,000 antibody candidates in 4 hours, screens them computationally for stability and specificity, and identifies the top 50 for experimental validation. Applied to SARS-CoV-2 variants, AbDesign produced broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies with sub-nanomolar affinity against 8 variants including immune-evasive strains. The pipeline reduces antibody development from 18 months to 6 weeks while achieving 73% experimental success rate.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle Optimization for CNS Gene Therapy Delivery
abstract: Delivering therapeutic nucleic acids to the central nervous system remains a major challenge for gene therapy. We developed a systematic screening approach for ionizable lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) optimized for CNS delivery, testing 1,200 lipid formulations in a mouse brain transfection assay. Machine learning optimization identified 3 lead LNP formulations with 8-fold improved brain penetration compared to standard MC3 LNPs. The lead LNP (CNS-LNP7) achieves 67% transfection efficiency in cortical neurons after intrathecal injection with minimal liver off-targeting. Applied to CRISPR-Cas9 delivery for huntingtin knockdown in HD mice, CNS-LNP7 reduced mutant HTT protein by 84% in striatum and improved motor function.

title: Spatial Transcriptomics Maps Tumor Microenvironment Architecture in Breast Cancer
abstract: Tumor-immune interactions are spatially organized within the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet bulk RNA-seq cannot capture this spatial context. We applied 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics to 245 treatment-naive breast cancer biopsies, creating a spatial atlas of TME organization across 4 molecular subtypes. We identified 8 spatially defined TME archetypes that predict pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy with 91% accuracy. A novel 'immune exclusion border' (IEB) spatial pattern, present in 35% of triple-negative breast cancers, is associated with resistance to anti-PD-L1 therapy. The IEB is maintained by CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling from cancer-associated fibroblasts. Targeting this axis restored T cell infiltration and sensitized tumors to immunotherapy in patient-derived xenografts.
